subject: Post-call: RAG validation plan & evaluation artifacts for Salix Bio
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Shaw <ben.shaw@salixbio.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: RAG validation plan & evaluation artifacts for Salix Bio

Hi Ben — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights:
- Goal: replace fragile search-based answers in Salix's internal protocols UI with grounded RAG answers and a compact citation UX.
- Primary risk: hallucination for rare assay protocols; dataset size ~120k docs, many short PDFs.
- Success metrics you care about: precision@1 (answer exactness), grounding_rate (cite provided doc), and latency < 350ms P50.

Proposed validation plan (short):
1) Eval harness & prompt set: we prepared an initial prompt set and sampling strategy (attached). We suggest 600 test prompts covering 1) routine SOP lookups, 2) edge-case protocol exceptions, 3) multi-step troubleshooting.
2) Retrieval configuration: vector store (FAISS IVFFlat) with dense-embedding nearest-neighbor k=12, prefilter by metadata (doc_type, assay_id), shard by year for faster cold-starts.
3) Reranker: start with a cross-encoder reranker (electra-base fine-tuned) as the high-precision pass; fallback to bi-encoder similarity for high throughput.
4) Model choices: run parallel comparisons: redwood/gpt-medium-quant (fast, 8-bit quant) and a higher-capacity open-llama-13B variant for quality sensitive flows.
5) Grounding metrics & thresholds: aim for grounding_rate >= 0.88 and precision@1 >= 0.82 on the core SOP subset; set an automatic fallback to source-snippet display if grounding_confidence < 0.6.

Deliverables I attached/linked:
- salix_rag_eval_promptset_v1.zip (prompt templates, 600 test cases) [attachment stub]
- Quick benchmark export (CSV) with sample latencies and token costs (salix_bench_results_q2.csv) [attachment stub]
- Shared Drive: evaluation plan + runbook (link below).

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you share one sample PDF (an SOP that frequently caused wrong answers) so we can sanity-run the first retrieval config?
- Agree to a 45-minute follow-up next Tue (May 25) where we’ll walk initial runs and choose quantization profile.

If you agree, I’ll spin up a small pilot (dedicated evaluation job) and drop the first dashboard by EOD Monday.

Best,

Thanks for the quick reply and the SOP-42 sample — received it and shared with the retrieval team. Short answers to your questions: 

- Retrieval k tradeoff: raising k improves recall (more candidates for the reranker) which tends to increase precision@1 after reranking, but adds retrieval + rerank latency proportionally. Our pilot config (k=12) targets a good middle ground; we expect P50 latency delta of ~30–60ms vs k=6 when using local FAISS shards. If latency is critical we can use k=6 for low-latency flows and k=12 for accuracy-first flows.

- Cost delta: rough ballpark for generation cost per 1k tokens (in pilot config): redwood/gpt-medium-quant ≈ $0.12; open-llama-13B ≈ $0.35. These are subject to batching and KV-cache reuse; we’ll provide a detailed estimate in the dashboard.

Action items I’m taking now:
- Marcus will run a quick reranker ablation (cross-encoder vs bi-encoder) on SOP-42 and return precision@1 and grounding_rate.
- I’ll queue a short pilot (2k queries) on the two model variants and post results to the Drive by Monday EOD.
- Scheduling: confirmed Tue May 25, 11am ET — invite to come from my calendar.

Olga

Hi Ben / Olga — quick results from the SOP-42 ablation (first pass):

- Setup: 120 seed queries derived from the SOP (mix of lookup + multi-step). Retrieval: FAISS IVFFlat, k=12; embeddings from redwood/embed-base.
- Cross-encoder reranker (electra-base fine-tuned): precision@1 = 0.86, grounding_rate = 0.90, avg additional latency ~75ms.
- Bi-encoder + dot-product (no reranker): precision@1 = 0.70, grounding_rate = 0.74, latency savings ~120ms vs cross-encoder.

Recommendation: for the SOP flow we should use cross-encoder as primary (meets grounding target) and expose a low-latency toggle that uses bi-encoder for <200ms callers. Also we should add a simple grounding_confidence calibration that checks overlap between top snippet tokens and model citation tokens; when confidence < 0.55, surface the raw snippet with a conservative answer template.

I pushed the first CSV to the Drive (salix_bench_results_q2.csv) and added a short notes doc in the folder. Linking here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_Example

Happy to walk through the ablation at Tue’s call.

-Marcus Lin
Applied ML, Inference Optimizations | Redwood Inference
